A kid's travel guide

Den Haag

Sun, sand and secret palaces on the North Sea coast of the Netherlands — here's everything worth knowing before you go.

Country
The Netherlands
Dutch name
Den Haag
Province
South Holland

Den Haag (in English: The Hague) is a city by the sea in the Netherlands. It is not the capital — that's Amsterdam! Den Haag is the capital of the province of South Holland, and it's where the Dutch parliament and government meet. It has also been home to the royal family since 1831, and it's where countries from all over the world come to sort out big problems peacefully.

It's also home to a real beach, a shrunk-down version of the whole country, and one of the most famous paintings in the world. Not bad for one city.

Good to know before you go

  • Pay by card. Almost everyone in the Netherlands pays by card, even for small things. Some shops don't take cash at all — bring a bank card.
  • Watch for bikes. There are bike paths (fietspaden) everywhere in Den Haag. Always look both ways before you cross — bikes are fast and quiet.
  • Emergency number: 112. If something goes wrong, call 112 for police, fire or an ambulance. It's free, day or night.

Getting around by train, tram & bus

Den Haag has trains, trams and buses that can take you almost anywhere. Trains run on the national railway NS (Nederlandse Spoorwegen) — their free NS app shows train times and sells tickets. Trams and buses in the city are run by HTM. The free 9292 app shows times and routes for trains, trams and buses all in one place, so you can always see exactly when the next one leaves.

Weather & best time to visit

Den Haag has typical Dutch weather: mild summers, cool winters, and rain is possible any time of year. Summer (June to August) is best for the beach, but a rain jacket is always a good idea — even on a sunny day, the wind off the North Sea can surprise you.

Good to know

A few practical things before you pack your bag.

Best time to visit

Summer is best for the beach, but Den Haag's museums and palaces are great to visit any time of year.

Pack a jacket

The North Sea wind is no joke, even in summer. Bring a windbreaker for the beach and the pier.

Getting around town

Trams and buses (HTM) go everywhere in Den Haag. Tap a bank card on board to pay for your ride.

English works fine

Almost everyone in the Netherlands speaks great English, so it's easy to ask for help or order food.
